newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on "inappropriate" profits.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on "inappropriate" profits.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Thursday on news that 163 executives and major shareholders in 89 listed firms had been ordered to return "inappropriate" profits reaped through speculative trade, brokers said.
The weighted index ended down 56.92 points or 0.87 percent at 6,494.34. Turnover was a modest T$39.57 billion.
The stock exchange on Thursday ordered the guilty executives and shareholders to return to their firms some T$21.6 million in what it called "inapprpriate" quick-turnaround profits.
"Sentiment already was weak from Wednesday's fall. This news exacerbated things," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment.
The market slid from the open, beset by weak confidence triggered by Wednesday's 0.98 percent fall.

The heavily weighted financial sectors fell by 1.44 percent on intensifying margin call pressure. Central Insurance lost 3.03 percent or T$2 to T$64, and Chiao Tung Bank dropped 2.07 percent or T$1.50 to T$71.

Fundamentals-backed electronics mounted the strongest defence, losing only 0.27 percent. Macronix, backed by impressive January-September profit reports, gained T$1.10 or 3.05 percent to close at T$37.20.
The market's inability to reach new peaks after hitting a 1996 high on October 5 was an underlying cause for the heavy disappointment and associated selling on Wednesday and Thursday, brokers added.
"Once it became apparent the index had little upside room, investors showed they would rather take profits and wait for the next bull run," said Chen Han-chung of Yungli Securities.
Brokers saw near-term support at 6,450 but said Friday's trading range likely would be capped at 6,550.
